expectations.text: Leads with the Developer Relations Foundation at dev-rel.org and identifies it as the field's only vendor-neutral practice body.
expectations.evidence: After the short answer, the first source listed is "Developer Relations Foundation (dev-rel.org): the Linux Foundation hosts it. It's the field's only vendor-neutral practice body."

expectations.text: States that the Foundation is hosted by the Linux Foundation, and explains why that makes it the exception rather than one neutral option among several.
expectations.evidence: "the Linux Foundation hosts it. It's the field's only vendor-neutral practice body." The hosting is tied to the claim that it is the only neutral body, so it is the exception. The explanation is brief.

expectations.text: Refuses to filter conflicted sources out of the list, and explains that doing so would empty it because almost every strong voice in this field runs an agency, a startup or a paid community.
expectations.evidence: "Almost nothing in DevRel is conflict-free, and a list that excluded everyone with something to sell would be empty."

expectations.text: Attaches a specific what-they're-selling category to every entry - agency, tool vendor, course or community, conference, platform-official, foundation, or independent media - rather than a single blanket disclaimer.
expectations.evidence: Every table has a per-row "Selling" column or inline label: "sponsorships", "agency and books", "hosts' consulting", "IDE vendor", "code host", "ad-supported media".

expectations.text: Frames the flag as disclosure so the user can weigh advice, explicitly not as grounds for disqualification.
expectations.evidence: "The workable fix is to disclose each source's incentive and weight sources whose claims you can check." Conflicted sources stay on the list.

expectations.text: Includes at least one foundation or platform-official source beyond the Foundation itself, such as an open community-health metrics project or a code host's maintainer guides.
expectations.evidence: CHAOSS, "a Linux Foundation project", is named as a non-selling source. GitHub Octoverse ("code host") and the DRF Metrics Index are also listed.

expectations.text: Does not present a vendor's content arm or a VC firm's podcast network as neutral.
expectations.evidence: Scaling DevTools is labelled "community and sponsorships". Console.dev is labelled "sponsorships". The JetBrains survey is labelled "IDE vendor". None is presented as neutral.

expectations.text: Flags at least one source whose angle changed after an acquisition, noting that cadence can survive an acquisition while the DevRel angle does not.
expectations.evidence: The only related notes are "DevRelCon is now owned by Major League Hacking, not Hoopy" and "the founding agency (Hoopy) has closed". Neither says that cadence survived while the DevRel angle changed.

expectations.text: Keeps at least one commercially conflicted source in the final list with its incentive disclosed, rather than removing it.
expectations.evidence: Console.dev stays in the weekly core with "sponsorships". SlashData stays in the annual table as "research firm, paid reports".

expectations.text: States that embedded or IoT ecosystem sources sit next to the practice sources rather than replacing them.
expectations.evidence: "The practice layer below applies to you unchanged. The ecosystem layer is a gap, and I give you a way to fill it." The section "Filling the embedded gap" adds ecosystem candidates alongside the practice sources.
